checkpoints.quote:
Normal session activity — the user queries settlement allocations, edits numeric grid cells, invokes actions. All XHRs return 200. A token refresh (/api/security/token/refresh) succeeds at one point.
2. **Gap of ~4.16 hours** (timestamp jumps from 1789182813 to 1789197792) with no breadcrumbs
checkpoints.reason: The analysis clearly conveys the two-phase split (all 200s, then a ~4-hour-10-minute gap, then all 401s) with the correct timestamps and gap duration.

checkpoints.quote: the frontend code assumes API responses always succeed and immediately reads properties (.rows, .returnProperties, .length, .sort) off the response body without checking for an error/failure state. When the backend returns 401 with an empty body (likely because the auth/session token had expired during the long idle gap), the response data is undefined, and the unguarded property access throws.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis identifies the TypeError as a symptom of unhandled 401s and names the systemic lack of 401 handling as the underlying defect, matching the expected point.

checkpoints.quote: Correlated with these 401s, four uncaught TypeErrors fire in quick succession: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rows') ×2, Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'returnProperties'), Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length'), Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sort')
checkpoints.reason: The analysis lists all four earlier sentry.event breadcrumbs plus the .sort event and frames them as one systemic gap rather than separate bugs.

checkpoints.quote: We only see one successful refresh before the gap, and no refresh attempt visible after it.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis correctly identifies the single token refresh before the gap and the absence of any refresh after it.

checkpoints.quote: the event's environment tag and _dsc.environment both say "Production", but every URL in the event (page URL, all API calls) is bank-uat.example.com — a UAT host. This is a real conflict in the data, not just Tom's suspicion; it needs confirming before this is logged/escalated as a production incident.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis identifies the Production-vs-UAT conflict clearly but hedges with 'if this is actually a UAT-only issue mislabeled as Production' and 'needs confirming' rather than definitively concluding the environment is misconfigured and polluting production alerting.

The analysis never mentions the transaction/culprit field being /settlements/run/8214, the discrepancy with the /payments/batch/actions URL, or the implication that the transaction name is stale and misdirects Sentry grouping.

checkpoints.quote: Stack trace is unsymbolicated — function names are minified (Y, V, H, ie.project, etc.) and Sentry's own symbolication attempts failed (scraping_attempts show DNS resolution failures for bank-uat.example.com...google.internal, i.e. Sentry couldn't fetch source maps from this host). So the exact source line/component responsible cannot be identified from this event alone.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis conveys that the stack cannot identify the failing component due to missing source maps, failed scraping attempts, and minified frame names.
The analysis never mentions that release and dist are both null in the Sentry event, nor the implication that the event cannot be tied to a specific build.

checkpoints.quote: Root cause of the 401s themselves is not shown. The event doesn't reveal whether the token-refresh mechanism failed to fire after the idle period, whether the refresh token itself had expired, or whether the backend session was invalidated some other way.
checkpoints.reason: The analysis notes the empty 401 bodies and explicitly states the event cannot distinguish between token expiry, revocation, or server-side session drop.

checkpoints.quote: likely because the auth/session token had expired during the long idle gap
checkpoints.reason: The analysis presents token expiry during the idle period as a likely mechanism, grounded in the pre-gap refresh, the 4-hour gap, and post-gap 401s, using 'likely' to mark it as inference.
The analysis does not address the 780 KB InvokeAction response, the Referer being a new-tab page, the browser/OS being ordinary, or the '401 OK' statusText wording in console messages.
The analysis never discusses the in_app flags on frames, the in_app_frame_mix 'in-app-only' metadata, or the point that this flag is not evidence the fault is in application code.

checkpoints.quote: Fix the response-handling gap at the HTTP client/interceptor or shared data-service level so that failed (401 or otherwise non-2xx) responses don't leave callers dereferencing undefined — rather than only guarding the single .sort() call
checkpoints.reason: The analysis covers fixing 401 handling centrally, fixing the environment, and getting source maps, but omits redirect-to-sign-in, setting release/dist, correcting the stale transaction name, and the explicit statement that a null guard would hide the blank screen without fixing the root cause.
The analysis explicitly rejects the null guard as the fix, calling it a mask, and identifies the 401 handling gap as the real issue.
The analysis flags the UAT URL conflict and questions whether it should be treated as a production incident rather than asserting it is production.
The analysis never states the error occurred on /settlements/run/8214 or references settlements run 8214 as the screen.
The analysis explicitly states the exact source line/component cannot be identified and does not name any specific application source file, component, method, or line number as the fault location.
The analysis does not blame the 780 KB response, slow network, browser, browser version, or operating system.
The analysis attributes the 401s to likely token expiry during idle, not to an attack, intrusion, permissions misconfiguration, or server outage.
The analysis explicitly states there are 'no breadcrumbs' during the gap and does not describe any activity or errors during it.
